name: Domain Selection
description: A systematic methodology for choosing where to look before what to find. Domain selection is the foundation of innovation — it answers the fundamental question: Where should I look before I decide what to find? Uses three criteria: Interest, Knowledge, and Research Accessibility.

name: Dominant Design
description: Utterback-Abernathy (1975; Mastering the Dynamics of Innovation, 1994): the point where competing product architectures converge into one accepted standard configuration. Before it (era of ferment): many competing architectures, high product-innovation rate, firms compete on features. After it emerges: product innovation collapses, process innovation rises sharply, competition shifts to cost/efficiency/scale, entry barriers rise. The dominant design is rarely the technically best option -- it wins via network effects/installed base (QWERTY, VHS over Betamax), standards-body lock-in, control of complementary assets, or being first credible-enough solution. Diagnostic use: is this market still in ferment or has a design already won; what would make a design durable regardless of merit; is the team competing on the right axis (features pre-convergence vs cost/scale post-convergence is a common fatal misread).

name: ESG Due Diligence Framework
description: VentureESG 9-part assessment for venture-backed companies. Includes materiality assessment to focus resources on highest-impact ESG factors per business type.

name: ESG Materiality Assessment
description: Determines which ESG factors are material for a specific business type. A SaaS company focuses on data privacy and governance; a hardware company adds supply chain and materials.

name: Effectuation
description: Saras Sarasvathy entrepreneurship theory: expert entrepreneurs use means-based logic (bird in hand, affordable loss, lemonade, crazy quilt, pilot in the plane) rather than goal-based prediction.

name: Emotional Intelligence in Leadership
description: Five components: self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, social skills (Goleman)

name: Engineering Ethics in Leadership
description: Public health, safety, welfare considerations — ABET-aligned ethical reasoning in technical contexts

name: Entrepreneurial Method

name: Feedback loops

name: Klein's Triple Path Model
description: Gary Klein's account of how insight arrives: an unexpected shift to a better story. Three paths, each altering the anchors that frame a situation. Connections add a new anchor (intersectional innovation, e.g. telephone plus computer). Contradictions replace an old anchor when an anomaly cannot be dismissed. Creative Desperation overturns a fixed assumption when stuck (the Mann Gulch fire, 1949).

name: Knowns and Unknowns Matrix Framework
description: A systematic knowledge categorization and uncertainty analysis framework that transforms blind spot discovery into a structured process. Uses a 2x2 matrix to categorize information based on awareness and knowledge dimensions, enabling systematic identification of known knowns, known unknowns, unknown knowns, and unknown unknowns.

name: Legal Due Diligence Framework

name: OODA Loop
description: John Boyd's decision cycle: Observe, Orient, Decide, Act, repeated continuously. Whoever cycles through the loop faster and with better orientation than an opponent operates inside the opponent's decision cycle, creating confusion and advantage. Orient is the pivotal phase, shaped by experience, culture, analysis and synthesis, and new information.
jtbd_anchor: When I face a fast-changing or adversarial situation, I want to cycle through observation, orientation, decision, and action faster than conditions change, so I can stay ahead of events and opponents.

Well-defined asks how to solve this specific problem and is the only kind that can actually be solved. Each type carries a different time frame and degree of uncertainty.

name: The Innovation Landscape
description: A two by two of uncertainty against risk used to choose where to play. Risk has statistics and probabilities (the insurance industry); uncertainty has neither (no statistic predicted Russia invading Ukraine). The entrepreneur's quadrant is low risk, high uncertainty: uncertainty is the entrepreneur's friend because if it were certain, incumbents would already be there. High uncertainty plus high risk belongs to governments. Uncertainty splits into technological (will it work) and market (will the market still be there).

name: Wallas Four-Stage Model of the Creative Process

Popularly rendered as four stages (Preparation, Incubation, Illumination, Verification) but actually five: Wallas described Intimation, the fringe-consciousness feeling that an illumination is imminent, between Incubation and Illumination. The model operates across three levels of consciousness and the stages overlap rather than running in a strict line.
